title: RiverBank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
summary: Introductory discovery focused on data residency, GDPR/HIPAA concerns, and whether Redwood hosted, dedicated, or private deployment fits RiverBank's compliance needs. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO docs, BAA details, dedicated pricing, and schedule technical deep dive / PoC timeline.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
action_items: Alex Monroe: Share SOC2 and ISO27001 reports and security pack - due 2025-11-03
Priya Shah: Prep dedicated sizing estimate + pricing for 3-node reserved pool - due 2025-11-05
Javier Ortega: Send current data flow diagram and list of endpoints that process customer data - due 2025-11-04
next_steps: Redwood to send security package and BAA template
Schedule technical deep dive with RiverBank infra team (Priya) week of 2025-11-10
Customer to provide high-level compliance requirements doc and timeline for decision (Susan/Mark)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-29 16:00 UTC | Duration: 37 minutes | Attendees: Alex Monroe, Priya Shah (Redwood); Mark Ellis, Susan Park, Javier Ortega (RiverBank)

Summary: Quick intros, then deep dive on data residency and compliance constraints for RiverBank's LLM use cases. Focus on whether hosted API is acceptable or if they need dedicated or private deployments because of GDPR/HIPAA and internal logging restrictions.

[00:00] Alex Monroe: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the account exec on this one. With me is Priya our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?

[00:12] Mark Ellis: Good, thanks Alex. Mark here, CIO. We appreciate you fitting us in.

[00:18] Susan Park: Hi, Susan from compliance. I'll jump in on questions around GDPR and retention.

[00:24] Javier Ortega: And Javier, DevOps. I'll handle the nitty gritty infra questions.

[00:30] Alex Monroe: Great. Quick agenda — confirm use cases, walk through redwood hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private), discuss GDPR/HIPAA implications and logging, then agree next steps. Sound good?

[00:41] Mark Ellis: Yes. Our team is evaluating an LLM assistant for customer support and internal docs. The big blockers for us are data residency for EU customers, potential HIPAA if we extend to health-related accounts, and strict logging rules — we can't have raw PII in third-party logs.

[00:56] Priya Shah: Understood. From a high level, Redwood has three deployment modes: our Hosted API (fastest to deploy), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool for a customer, isolated tenancy on our infra), and Private which is VPC or on-prem managed deployments. Each has different compliance and residency guarantees.

[01:15] Susan Park: Can you clarify what "hosted" means for data residency? If we use hosted, where is the data stored and processed?

[01:22] Alex Monroe: Sure, hosted routes requests through our global control plane and processing happens in regions we operate. For EU data we have EU regions and can route traffic to avoid leaving EU — but it's still within Redwood's managed environment. Some regulators want customer-managed networks or a BAA for HIPAA which hosted alone may not satisfy.

[01:40] Javier Ortega: And how about logs? If an end-user submits a ticket that contains personal data, does that get logged on Redwood's side?

[01:47] Priya Shah: By default we capture request metadata and diagnostic logs for observability, but we have configs: you can disable request payload logging, enable redaction, or use prefix-only logging. For Dedicated and Private we can turn off payload retention entirely and route logs to your own blob storage or KMS-backed sinks.

[02:05] Susan Park: Do you offer a BAA? HIPAA is a possibility for us, so we need to know if Redwood will sign as a Business Associate.

[02:11] Alex Monroe: Yes, Redwood offers a BAA for Dedicated and Private customers; we can discuss terms. For hosted customers, it's case-by-case and typically requires additional controls. We'll include our BAA template in the security pack.

[02:25] Mark Ellis: For GDPR, we need EU data residency and the ability to demonstrate where processing happens and have audit logs that we control. Does the Hosted option give us that granularity?

[02:34] Priya Shah: Hosted can provide region-based routing and a compliance report showing where processing occurred, but the level of control is less than Dedicated or Private. With Dedicated you get a reserved pool physically located in a specific cloud region and we provide audit logs and longer retention choices. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you the most control — all inference happens inside your VPC or on-prem environment and logs never land in our managed systems unless you want them to.

[02:55] Javier Ortega: You mentioned KMS/HSM earlier. We use AWS KMS and are exploring external HSMs for key management. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS so keys never leave our control?

[03:04] Priya Shah: Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and for on-prem we can integrate with HSMs. Note: for some models and quantized workflows, certain ephemeral keys are used in the runtime; we can make sure customer keys manage encryption at rest and in transit.

[03:22] Mark Ellis: How about SOC2 and ISO certifications? Our procurement requires SOC2 Type II.

[03:27] Alex Monroe: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and has ISO 27001. We'll attach the reports; Priya will include them in the security pack.

[03:34] Susan Park: On logging restrictions, we also have a policy that application logs cannot contain full credit card numbers or national IDs. Does Redwood provide redaction at ingestion?

[03:44] Priya Shah: We have configurable ingestion filters and PII scrubbing rules — regex-based and ML-based detectors. For Hosted we provide standard scrubbing and you can opt-in for stronger redaction, but for ultimate control Dedicated/Private allows you to own the scrubber entirely or send logs to your side before it's persisted.

[04:05] Javier Ortega: If we go hosted but need to mask payloads before they hit Redwood logs, can we do client-side redaction?

[04:11] Alex Monroe: Absolutely. Many customers implement client-side masking combined with prefix caching so the model still sees context without PII. We can share a best-practices guide.

[04:22] Mark Ellis: Another point: our legal team needs proof that data doesn't persist beyond X days and we can prove deletions on request. Is that supported?

[04:31] Priya Shah: Yes, data retention policies are configurable. Hosted default retention is short, but for regulated customers we can set retention to zero or implement guaranteed deletion workflows. Dedicated and Private give stronger SLAs around retention and deletion logs.

[04:46] Susan Park: For EU data subjects exercising rights, we need exports and deletion logs. Do you provide exportable audit trails?

[04:53] Priya Shah: We provide audit logs that you can export — with Dedicated we can give longer retention and a more detailed audit trail. Private deployments keep everything in your control for e-Discovery.

[05:04] Javier Ortega: On the technical side, how do we pin model versions and ensure rollbacks in case of quality regressions? We need reproducibility for compliance.

[05:13] Priya Shah: Redwood supports model version pinning and rollout policies — canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to previous versions. These are available across modes; in Hosted we maintain the control plane but you can pin by model hash and version. In Dedicated/Private you also control the model artifacts and image baselines.

[05:29] Mark Ellis: Is there any performance tradeoff when enabling strong redaction or routing through EU data centers? Our P50 latency goals are around 300ms for a typical 256-token request.

[05:38] Priya Shah: There's some overhead for redaction pre-processing and for routing to specific regions. For Dedicated in-region pools we can meet 300ms P50 easily for optimized local models; for Hosted EU we usually see slightly higher latencies because of multi-tenant routing but it's still in the low hundreds for many models. We'll run benchmarks in the PoC.

[05:57] Susan Park: A few compliance-specific questions: audit logging for who accessed what model, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, and separation of duties. How mature are those features?

[06:07] Alex Monroe: SSO with SAML and OIDC is supported. RBAC with role mapping is mature in our console, and we provide detailed access audit logs for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has role-based controls, but for strict separation Dedicated/Private is recommended.

[06:22] Javier Ortega: For the PoC, we'd want a small dedicated pool that only processes EU traffic and uses our KMS keys, plus the ability to disable payload logging. Is that feasible?

[06:31] Priya Shah: Yes, that's a standard PoC for banks. We can provision a 2-3 node dedicated pool in the EU with customer KMS integration and payload logging disabled. We'll need a short security checklist and network details.

[06:43] Mark Ellis: Timeline-wise, procurement wants vendor selection by end of Q4. We'd need pricing, security docs, and a short PoC this quarter.

[06:52] Alex Monroe: That aligns with our go-to-market. We'll get the SOC2/ISO and BAA and a dedicated pricing estimate to you within the next week. Priya will lead the technical deep dive and PoC coordination.

[07:03] Susan Park: One more: do you support data residency for backups and object stores? Backups must remain in-region.

[07:10] Priya Shah: Yes — for Dedicated and Private we ensure backups and model artifacts remain in-region and can be encrypted with your KMS. For Hosted we'll document the backup location and options, but Dedicated/Private offers stronger guarantees.

[07:24] Javier Ortega: Regarding logs that are needed for incident response, if we disable payload logging, how do we debug incidents? What's the trade-off?

[07:32] Priya Shah: We recommend hybrid: redact PII but retain enough operational metadata (hashes/prefixes) and structured traces to debug. For critical incidents, we can run a secure debug session with your team where payloads are temporarily captured under a stricter audit and then deleted.

[07:48] Mark Ellis: That could work. From a procurement perspective, will Redwood accept pen test reports or do you require your own assessments?

[07:56] Alex Monroe: We accept third-party pen test reports and have our own red team results. We'll include engagement details in the security pack.

[08:05] Susan Park: Are there any regulatory controls specific to financial services you highlight? Anything you do for banks by default?

[08:12] Priya Shah: For financial customers we offer hardened default configs: limited retention, region restriction, mandatory RBAC with MFA, and extra audit logging by default. We also have a controls matrix mapping to FFIEC-like requirements.

[08:25] Javier Ortega: Let's talk about network connectivity — do you support private connectivity like AWS PrivateLink or direct connect equivalents?

[08:33] Priya Shah: Yes, Dedicated and Private support PrivateLink/VPC endpoints and we can set up peering or direct connect for on-prem. We'll want to collect your network requirements for the PoC.

[08:44] Mark Ellis: Cost question: what's the delta between hosted and dedicated in rough terms? We understand it varies but a ballpark helps.

[08:52] Alex Monroe: Ballpark: Hosted is usage-based and typically lower upfront; Dedicated has a reserved capacity model — upfront commit leads to lower per-token cost and more predictable tail latency. For banks, Dedicated often makes sense for both cost predictability and compliance. We'll send a sample pricing model.

[09:07] Mark Ellis: One last compliance nuance — do you persist any derivatives that might be considered personal data, like embeddings or anonymized vectors? Some regs treat embeddings as re-identifiable.

[09:17] Priya Shah: We treat embeddings as potentially sensitive; retention is configurable and you can choose not to persist them on Redwood side. For Dedicated/Private, you can ensure embeddings are stored only in your controlled storage. We'll document our approach and recommendations.

[09:34] Alex Monroe: Okay, sounds like we're aligned on next steps. Priya, can you run through what you'll need from RiverBank to kick off the PoC?

[09:40] Priya Shah: Sure — high-level network diagram, a list of EU endpoints and sample traffic patterns, compliance checklist, and the KMS details for key integration. Also which model families you want to evaluate. Ideally a single point of contact for the infra setup — Javier looks like it might be you.

[09:54] Javier Ortega: Yep, I can be the contact. I'll put together the diagram and sample payloads, though we'll scrub PII before sending.

[10:03] Susan Park: We'll also prepare a one-page compliance requirement doc for your legal/security team.

[10:10] Alex Monroe: Great. We'll follow up with the security pack and BAA and a pricing estimate. Can we target delivery of those items by 2025-11-03?

[10:19] Mark Ellis: Yes that timeline works for us.

[10:23] Alex Monroe: Anything else before we wrap?

[10:27] Susan Park: One small question — do you have examples of banks using Redwood in EU-only deployments?

[10:33] Priya Shah: We do; we'll anonymize case studies for privacy but include a short reference set and a compliance mapping.

[10:41] Mark Ellis: Alright, thanks everyone.

[10:43] Alex Monroe: Thanks for your time. We'll send the docs and get the PoC scheduled.

Recap / Next steps: 1) Redwood to send SOC2/ISO reports and BAA template by 2025-11-03. 2) Priya to prepare dedicated sizing + pricing by 2025-11-05. 3) Javier to deliver network diagram and sample scrubbing approach by 2025-11-04. 4) Schedule technical deep dive week of 2025-11-10.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (product names like "KV cash" instead of KV cache), filler words and crosstalk present.
